name: Lumbini Pilgrimage Tour

difficulty.notes: Flat site; monastic zones are explored on foot, by bicycle or electric rickshaw.

duration_days.basis: Kathmandu to Kathmandu by air via Bhairahawa
duration_days.notes: 2 nights in Lumbini allows the Sacred Garden plus both monastic zones; a longer version adds Tilaurakot (ancient Kapilavastu) and other Greater Lumbini sites. Often combined with Chitwan (~4 h by road) or Pokhara.

itinerary.route: Kathmandu - Bhairahawa (Gautam Buddha International Airport, domestic flight) - Lumbini (~22 km); evening at the Sacred Garden
Maya Devi Temple, marker stone, Ashoka Pillar and Puskarini pond in the Sacred Garden; East and West Monastic Zones; World Peace Pagoda
itinerary.notes: Shoes removed in the temple; food and drinks left outside.

best_seasons.notes: Terai heat and monsoon make May-September uncomfortable (travel-site guidance). Buddha Jayanti (Buddha's birthday, Apr/May full moon) draws pilgrims.

permits.name: Lumbini Development and Conservation Fee (Sacred Garden / Maya Devi Temple), per day
permits.applies_to: other foreign nationals (non-SAARC); SAARC + Myanmar NPR 700; Indian NPR 80; Nepali NPR 20; waived for monks, nuns, persons with disabilities and residents of the three surrounding districts

guide_requirements: No legal guide requirement. Drone flights need permission from the District Administration Office, CAAN and the Lumbini Development Trust.

flights: Kathmandu - Bhairahawa (Gautam Buddha International Airport), domestic ~30-35 min
logistics.notes: Tickets can be bought in cash, by QR code or online at tickets.lumbinidevtrust.gov.np.

highlights: Maya Devi Temple at the birthplace of Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha)
Ashoka Pillar erected by Emperor Ashoka (inscription identifying the birthplace)
International monasteries in the East and West Monastic Zones
risks: Fog can delay winter flights to Bhairahawa
unverified: Fee change date: the Lumbini Development Trust page shows NPR 1,000 for other foreigners; news reports (May 2026) say the rise from NPR 700 took effect 1 May 2026. NTB's page still shows the old NPR 700, and several travel blogs show NPR 500 (outdated).
UNESCO inscription year (1997) and Ashoka Pillar date (249 BC) are from a travel site only.
Avoid-season guidance is from travel sites.
